target_paper_title: Neptune-X: Active X-to-Maritime Generation for Universal Maritime Object Detection

gold_annotations.topic: This paper studies maritime object detection under limited annotated data and poor generalization across maritime attributes such as object category, viewpoint, location, and imaging environment. It focuses on improving detector training through controllable maritime scene generation and synthetic sample selection tailored to maritime scenarios.
gold_annotations.golden_gap: The paper argues that maritime detection datasets are costly to collect and annotate and are imbalanced across important semantic attributes, which hurts generalization in rare or difficult settings. Traditional augmentation only remixes existing images and cannot create new semantics, while existing diffusion and layout-to-image methods do not explicitly model object-water interactions, often producing semantically inconsistent or physically implausible maritime scenes. The paper also argues that prior generative augmentation methods overlook that synthetic samples differ in downstream training utility, so generated data are not selected in a task-aware way.
gold_annotations.golden_method: The proposed method, Neptune-X, is a unified generation-selection framework. Its generation component, X-to-Maritime, extends Stable Diffusion with multi-condition guidance over text, object layouts, and water-surface conditions, and introduces a Bidirectional Object-Water Attention module to model interactions between objects and aquatic surroundings for more realistic scene synthesis. Its selection component uses Attribute-correlated Training Difficulty Factors and Attribute-dependent Active Sampling to score generated images by detector accuracy weighted by maritime attributes such as viewpoint, location, environment, and category, then selects high-value synthetic samples for detector training.
gold_annotations.gold_experiment: The experiments build and use the Maritime Generation Dataset, described as the first dataset tailored for generative maritime learning, with 11,900 samples spanning object categories, viewpoints, locations, and imaging environments. The paper evaluates both image generation and downstream object detection, using metrics including FID, CAS, YOLO Score, mAP, and mAP50. It compares Neptune-X or its generated data against prior controllable generation methods such as LayoutDiff, GLIGEN, InstDiff, and RC-L2I, and also compares the proposed active sampling strategy against multiple active learning baselines. Additional ablations study the Bidirectional Object-Water Attention components and the contribution of different attribute-dimensional difficulty factors.
